dw1-108-of-128-qubits-used: Experimental results, p.2: states 108 of 128 qubits worked and were used; Supp. II, p.7 repeats it.
dw1-random-pm1-couplings: Experimental results, p.2: each coupler set to +1 or -1 at random. 'Very rough landscape' is attributed to the authors in the value and is descriptive of the setup.
dw1-local-fields-zero-main: Experimental results, p.2: all hi = 0 for most data shown; data with fields is in the supplement (Figs. 5, 11, 29).
dw1-sizes-instances-runs: Experimental results, p.2: N = 8 to 108, 1000 instances per size, M = 1000 runs per instance; the three quotes read in context.
dw1-run-protocol-5us: Methods, p.6: 2.5 s cooling after programming, then 1000 runs at tf = 5 us.
dw1-schedule-ghz: Methods, p.6: 0.4 GHz temperature, A(0) about 5 GHz going to zero, B(tf) about 5 GHz.
dw1-temperature-20mk-p9: Supp. III.B, p.9: device temperature 20 mK (0.4 GHz), consistent with the 0.4 GHz in Methods. Note: Supp. VII, p.22 says 17 mK (see dw1-temperature-17mk-p22).
total-annealing-time-definition: Scaling, p.4: Rtf defined as tf times R, with R the repetitions to find the ground state at least once with 99% probability.
repetitions-formula-p099: Scaling, p.4: Rp = log(1-p)/log(1-s) with p = 0.99; derived in Supp. VI.B (Eq. 6).
scaling-only-intrinsic-annealing-time: Scaling, p.4: only intrinsic annealing time counted, not programming or readout overhead.
dw-extrapolation-not-asymptotic-5us-subo: Scaling, p.4-5: authors caution that extrapolating the device scaling will not give the true asymptotic scaling, since 5 us is suboptimal; Supp. VI.B and Fig. 27 back it. A caveat on their own result.
open-question-sqa-better-than-sa-class: Scaling, p.5: the authors name as an open question, left to future work, for which problem class SQA beats SA; it bounds what their finding (SQA scales slightly worse on these instances) covers.
sa-methods-beta-schedule: Methods, p.6: Metropolis, local spin flips, beta increased linearly from 0.1 to 3.
spin-dynamics-o3-model: Methods, p.6: the SD model is defined with O(3) unit vectors and the sign of the z-component as the Ising value.
ground-state-energies-exact-algorithms: Methods, p.6: reference ground state energies from exact belief propagation and divide-and-conquer; the quote is cut but the sentence is complete.
chimera-unit-cell-k44: Supp. Fig. 1 caption p.7 and Section II: 4x4 unit cells of eight qubits, K4,4 inside each cell.
chimera-simulation-sizes: Supp. II, p.7: L = 1 to 8, N = 8L^2 = 8 ... 512; says 'typically', and the value does too.
sa-multispin-coding-64: Supp. III.A, p.8: multi-spin coding, 64 simulations in parallel on one core.
sqa-discrete-vs-continuous-time-codes: Supp. III.B, p.8: both continuous and discrete time codes; discrete one uses cluster updates in imaginary time, typically 64 slices.
four-exact-solvers-list: Supp. III.C, p.9: the four exact solvers are listed as quoted.
single-spin-flip-error-fix-definition: Supp. IV.D, p.12: the error reduction scheme is described (check each spin once, flip the one that lowers energy most); it is the procedure applied in Fig. 14.
copula-definition-and-limits: Supp. V.A, p.13: Eq. (1) defines c = f/(f1 f2); independent gives 1, perfect correlation gives a delta function. The quotes omit the equation but the passage has it.
geometric-mean-failure-rate-definition: Supp. V.C, p.15: geometric means of failure rates define the averaged s for scaling plots, with the derivation in the same passage.
tree-decomposition-three-properties: Supp. VI.A, p.17: the three properties are the definition as the paper gives it.
spin-glass-server-200-spin-limit: Supp. VI.A, p.18: the spin glass server limited them to 200 spins; they say it would be interesting to test for a crossover. A stated limit on their biqmac timings.
repetition-formula-assumes-uncorrelated: Supp. VI.B, p.18: the formula assumes uncorrelated repetitions; the paper adds that 15% of device instances show correlations.
dw-no-optimum-annealing-time-found: Supp. VI.B, p.18 (Fig. 28): no minimum found, so device timings are only upper bounds on the optimal time. The limit is the stated conclusion; the Fig. 28 observation is for typical N = 108 data.
dw-data-in-transient-regime-no-speedup-c: Supp. VI.C, p.20: the authors say their data is in the initial transient regime and cannot support extrapolation or a speedup determination.
speedup-detection-needs-optimal-times: Supp. VI.C, p.19: optimal times needed for a valid speedup conclusion; device times are only upper bounds, giving underestimated scaling.
gap-method-beta-and-gamma-steps: Supp. VII, p.20-21: annealed from Gamma = 3 in steps of 0.1 with the continuous time algorithm at beta = 100 and 200.
gap-estimates-are-upper-bounds: Supp. VII, p.22: all gaps shown are upper bounds for the gap to the lowest excited state, since the fit can pick up a higher gap when the gap is very small.

theory_low.tunneling-element-order-gamma-d: Supp. IV.C, p.10: a perturbative argument, stated without derivation or conditions. Not a proved result.
theory_low.free-qubits-hypercube-energy-lowering: Supp. IV.C, p.11: first-order perturbation theory for the simplest hypercube case, stated and cited ([12,41,42]), not proved here.
